meta.note: LLM-distilled seed routes — community knowledge synthesised from training data covering running blogs, Strava segments, Reddit threads, run club guides, and travel resources. Coordinates are approximate centroids; OSM pipeline adds precise geometry.

routes.name: Embarcadero to Crissy Field
routes.terrain_notes: Flat the entire way. Bay Trail with water on your right the whole run. Light signals only at the start near the Ferry Building — rest is car-free path.
routes.best_time: Early morning or evening. Weekday mornings quietest.
routes.safety: Well-lit, heavily used, very safe any time of day.
routes.avoid: Midday weekends — extremely crowded around Pier 39 and Fisherman's Wharf.
routes.signature: The best flat run in SF. Ferry Building to the Golden Gate Bridge base — you'll see the bridge get closer with every kilometre.

routes.name: Golden Gate Park Big Lap
routes.terrain_notes: Perimeter road (JFK + MLK drives) mostly flat, some gentle rollers in the Panhandle. JFK closed to cars permanently — fully car-free. MLK still has limited traffic on weekdays.
routes.best_time: Sunday mornings — the entire park road network is car-free 9am–6pm.
routes.safety: Safe throughout. Well-used. Some dark sections near Stow Lake after sunset.
routes.avoid: Narrow paths during Saturday afternoon crowds.
routes.signature: SF's favourite long run. Every local runner has a GGP lap story.

routes.name: Ocean Beach / Great Highway
routes.terrain_notes: Dead flat. Completely closed to cars — one of the longest car-free urban running corridors in the US. Exposed to Pacific wind — bring a layer.
routes.best_time: Any time. Sunrise is spectacular. Closed to cars permanently.
routes.safety: Very safe. Well-lit at night. Wind can be strong — plan to run into wind first.
routes.avoid: Thick SF fog can make visibility low — rare safety concern.
routes.signature: Fog rolling in off the Pacific as you run south. The most SF thing you can do.

routes.name: Batteries to Bluffs (Presidio)
routes.terrain_notes: Coastal bluff trail. Moderate hills — nothing extreme but you will feel it. Some stairs, mostly packed dirt path. Spectacular views of the bridge and Marin headlands.
routes.best_time: Morning — trail gets traffic later. Not lit at night.
routes.safety: Safe during day. No lighting — avoid after dark. Trail is narrow in sections.
routes.avoid: Wet conditions make some sections muddy and slippery.
routes.signature: The Presidio's coastal trail is one of the most beautiful urban runs in the world. Period.

routes.name: Crissy Field to Baker Beach
routes.terrain_notes: Crissy Field is flat restored wetland. Transitions to a gentle climb up to Baker Beach through the Presidio. Great combo of flat coastal + light trail.
routes.best_time: Morning. Crissy Field is famously cold and windy in afternoons.
routes.safety: Safe throughout. Popular with dog walkers.
routes.avoid: Nothing specific — one of SF's most forgiving routes.
routes.signature: Golden Gate Bridge close enough to touch. Kite surfers on Crissy Field. Baker Beach gives you the postcard photo.

routes.name: Bernal Heights Loop
routes.terrain_notes: 360-degree city views from the hilltop. Short but steep — proper hill training. Dirt trail with loose rock in sections. Off-leash dogs everywhere.
routes.best_time: Any time — hilltop catches the sun all day. Sunrise and sunset spectacular.
routes.safety: Safe, well-used. Avoid in heavy rain — muddy and slippery.
routes.avoid: Nothing dangerous but very exposed — cold and windy in winter.
routes.signature: Best bang-for-buck hill training in SF. Views of the entire Bay. Locals treat it as their backyard.

routes.name: Glen Canyon to Twin Peaks
routes.terrain_notes: One of the more technical urban runs in SF. Glen Canyon is a genuine canyon trail in the middle of the city. Transitions to paved road climb up Twin Peaks. Serious elevation.
routes.best_time: Morning. Twin Peaks is very exposed — fog and wind can be brutal midday.
routes.safety: Glen Canyon trail can be isolated. Run with a partner early or late.
routes.avoid: Avoid Glen Canyon in wet season — creek crossings become difficult.
routes.signature: You forget you're in a city. Then you summit Twin Peaks and the whole city is beneath you.

routes.name: Lands End Trail
routes.terrain_notes: Rugged coastal trail along the northwest tip of SF. Some technical sections with roots and uneven rock. Spectacular ocean views. Connects to Sutro Baths ruins at the end.
routes.best_time: Low tide reveals more of the rocky coastline. Morning for best light.
routes.safety: Some sections close to cliff edges — stay on marked trail. Not lit.
routes.avoid: Wet days make the path very slippery.
routes.signature: Raw, wild, feels nothing like the city 500m behind you. The Sutro Baths ruins are an unreal finish line.

routes.name: Marine Drive Full Loop
routes.terrain_notes: Completely flat. The Queen's Necklace arc from Nariman Point to Chowpatty. Promenade is wide and smooth. Some broken tile sections mid-2025 — getting repaired.
routes.best_time: 5:00–7:30 AM. Before heat and traffic. Pre-sunrise is magical — city lights on the curve of the bay.
routes.safety: Very safe early morning. Gets crowded 6:30am onwards. Excellent lighting.
routes.avoid: Post 9am — becomes a tourist walk, too crowded for running.
routes.signature: The most iconic run in India. Every serious Mumbai runner has done this. The curve of the bay at sunrise is unforgettable.

routes.name: Carter Road to Bandstand Loop
routes.terrain_notes: Flat coastal promenade with some gentle undulation near Bandra Fort. Entirely car-free on the promenade. Carter Road is the most popular running spot in Bandra by far.
routes.best_time: 5:30–7:30 AM. After 8am it gets busy with walkers and couples.
routes.safety: Very safe. Well-lit. Popular enough that you're never alone.
routes.avoid: Post-sunset — less lighting near Bandstand end, though still used.
routes.signature: Sea Link views at Bandstand. The old Portuguese fort at the end. Best stretch of running in Bandra.

routes.name: Worli Seaface
routes.terrain_notes: Flat promenade. Less famous than Marine Drive but calmer and often less crowded. Connects to the Worli end of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link.
routes.best_time: Early morning. Can be done as extension of Marine Drive for a longer run.
routes.signature: Quieter version of Marine Drive. Worli fishing village on one side, open sea on the other.

routes.name: Danda to Versova Beach Walk
routes.terrain_notes: Three beaches end to end — Danda, Juhu, Versova. Entirely flat, entirely sand. Hard sand near the waterline at low tide is ideal. Construction debris near VBSL in northern section (2025).
routes.best_time: Very early morning at low tide. 5:00–6:30 AM for hard sand conditions.
routes.safety: Safe early morning. Deserted after dark — avoid then.
routes.avoid: High tide — soft sand makes running very difficult. Monsoon — waves reach the beach.
routes.signature: Three Bollywood film locations in one run. Fishermen launching boats at dawn. Raw, unfiltered Mumbai.

routes.name: Powai Lake Loop
routes.terrain_notes: Gentle undulations around the lake. Road surface is good — IIT Bombay campus on one side, Hiranandani colony on the other. One of the most underrated runs in Mumbai.
routes.best_time: Early morning. Weekdays are quieter — less weekend jogger traffic.
routes.safety: Safe. Well-lit around Hiranandani. Some sections near IIT campus less busy after dark.
routes.avoid: Heavy rain — some sections flood near the lake edge.
routes.signature: Completely different energy from the coastal runs. Green, calm, almost feels like a hill station.

routes.name: Shivaji Park Circuit
routes.terrain_notes: Flat perimeter road around Mumbai's largest open ground. One of the oldest running spots in the city — Sachin Tendulkar trained cricket here. Concrete surface. Gets very crowded 6-8am.
routes.best_time: 5:00–6:00 AM for space. After 8:30 AM when the morning crowd thins.
routes.safety: Very safe. Always people around. Well-lit.
routes.avoid: 6:30–8:00 AM — shared with hundreds of walkers, cyclists and cricketers.
routes.signature: Mumbai's original public fitness ground. The morning crowd is an institution — every age, every fitness level.

routes.name: Mumbai Coastal Road Promenade
routes.terrain_notes: Brand new as of August 2025. Smooth, wide, dedicated path. Runs from Marine Lines to Worli — longer than Marine Drive itself. No traffic signals on the promenade path. Best surface in Mumbai.
routes.best_time: Any time — it's so new and well-maintained it's genuinely good at any hour.
routes.safety: Excellent. New infrastructure, good lighting, popular.
routes.avoid: Nothing — this is the best new running infrastructure in Mumbai.
routes.signature: The future of running in Mumbai. Longer, smoother, and more modern than Marine Drive. Will become the #1 run in the city within a year.

routes.name: Priyadarshini Park Loop (Malabar Hill)
routes.terrain_notes: Small park with a perimeter jogging track. Immaculate surface. Malabar Hill location means sea views over Marine Drive. Short but excellent for interval training.
routes.best_time: Early morning. Park opens at 5:30 AM.
routes.safety: Very safe, gated park with security.
routes.avoid: Evenings get busy with walkers — hard to maintain running pace.
routes.signature: Hidden gem. The Hanging Gardens and sea views make it feel like running on top of the world.
